newsitem.title: FRANCE: France plans fines for firms complying with Helms.
newsitem.headline: France plans fines for firms complying with Helms.

text.p: French government spokesman Alain Lamassoure said on Thursday the government had put forward a bill which proposed to fine French companies complying with United States sanctions laws against Cuba, Iran and Libya.

Lamassoure said French companies faced fines of between 100,000 and 500,000 French francs ($87,900) if they complied with or failed to tell French authorites of U.S. attempts to impose its Helms-Burton and d'Amato-Kennedy laws.
"It's a legal conflict between the two sides of the Atlantic," Lamassoure said at a news conference.

The decision came after the first cabinet meeting following President Jacques Chirac's return from a South American tour in which he challenged U.S. dominance in the region and sought to guarantee France and Europe a growing share in a powerful emerging market.
In what was seen as an apparent attack on the Helms-Burton law introduced last year, Chirac said on March 14 trade rules must be set and accepted by all countries.
The European Union strongly opposes the Helms-Burton law which stiffens U.S. trade sanctions on Communist-ruled Cuba.
